name: A Warden of the Horde

meta.previous: You Scream, I Scream... (Horde), Cairne's Hoofprint (quest)

summary: In Orgrimmar, Children's Week ends with Grunth's return to Orphan Matron Battlewail. After seeing the world with his guardian, the young orphan hopes to become a hero himself.

sections.title: An Orphan's Farewell
sections.body: After the adventures of Children's Week, Grunth thanks you for showing him more than he ever dreamed he would see. He remembers his parents' advice to rise above hardship and hopes to become a hero like you. His final request is to return home and tell the matron about your time together.

sections.title: Home to the Valley of Honor
sections.body: You return Grunth to Orphan Matron Battlewail at the orphanage in the Valley of Honor. In the new Horde, caring for the young is a profound duty, since war has left countless children without parents. Battlewail praises your compassion as the true measure of a Horde hero. Grunth parts with a beloved pet so you will remember the bond formed during your travels.

faq.q: What is the purpose of this quest?
faq.answer: This brings the Horde's Children's Week festivities to a close. Return Grunth and the Orcish Orphan Whistle to Orphan Matron Battlewail in the Valley of Honor.
Grunth is an orcish youth who lives at the Orgrimmar Orphanage in the Valley of Honor. During Children's Week, a Horde champion takes him across Kalimdor to see legendary figures and grand sights.

faq.q: What do I bring back to the matron?
faq.answer: Bring the Orcish Orphan Whistle to Orphan Matron Battlewail when Grunth is ready to return home.

faq.q: Who oversees the orphans in Orgrimmar?
faq.answer: Orphan Matron Battlewail oversees the Orgrimmar Orphanage in the Valley of Honor, where she devotes her life to sheltering and raising the Horde's war orphans.

faq.q: Why does Grunth want to return home?
faq.answer: His Children's Week outings are over, and Grunth wants to tell the matron about his adventures and the kind guardian who took him along.

faq.q: Why is Children's Week important to the Horde?
faq.answer: Decades of relentless warfare against demons, humans, and centaur have left countless Horde children without families. Children's Week gives warriors time away from the battlefield to honor the future generations of Durotar and beyond.

angles.text: For the Horde, strength means more than skill in battle. It also means protecting and uplifting the vulnerable who will one day carry the Warchief's banner.
As an orc, you know courage and honor matter. Showing compassion to an orphaned child like Grunth reflects the nobility Thrall seeks to instill in the new Horde.
